title: fix: hide offline community models faster
author: voodoohop
pr_body_excerpt:
- Hides a 100% failing community model after five attributable failures in 30 minutes plus a failed fresh probe
- Relists only monitor-hidden models after one hour, ten post-hide requests at 90% or better, and a passing probe
- Lets an owner-reported fix relist after one passing probe while preserving owner and maintainer hides
- Adds targeted exact-ID probing for hidden text and image models

Checks:
- Biome and Node syntax
- Monitor shell syntax
- Local hidden exact-ID probe against an isolated HTTP fixture

gist.headline: The garden spots wilted models
gist.blurb: The community-model gardener now notices a fully offline branch much sooner. After a careful fresh probe, broken listings step aside so healthier models can keep blooming.
gist.summary: Community monitoring now hides a model after five attributable failures within 30 minutes plus a failed fresh probe, adds exact-ID probes for hidden text and image models, and relists monitor-hidden models only after sustained recovery and a passing probe.
gist.impact: Users will encounter fewer fully failing community models, while recovered models return after an hour, ten 90%+ successful post-hide requests and a passing probe—or an owner-reported fix confirmed by a probe.
gist.visual_concept: Depict Polli as a gentle garden monitor inspecting a row of code-plants representing community text and image models. One wilted plant is carefully marked hidden after a tiny diagnostic probe, while healthy plants glow and a recovering plant is checked with a magnifying glass; use a cozy terminal and status lights to convey automated reliability monitoring.
